page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per thread. The compute resources are powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor spanning 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, alongside standard vector extensions (AVX, BMI2, and FMA), while AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced single-thread execution alongside throughput constraints inherent to a 4-vCPU footprint. The instance scored 1,426.0 points in Geekbench single-core and 2,681.08 in single-core stress-ng tests, both aligning with median results across tested systems. Multi-threaded processing yielded 3,257.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 6,021.53 in PassMark CPU tests, reflecting lower-quartile performance for high-concurrency tasks. Memory performance tests showed write throughput of 28.03 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 2,030.58 in the average tier, with large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 38.56 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration contains no local NVMe storage and no auxiliary hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Network provisioning does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring cloud storage and external routing to be managed separately. In qualitative terms, the server provides cost-efficient access to high memory density without the baseline overhead of larger core counts, making it suitable for memory-heavy services that do not saturate high vCPU volumes.

Target workloads for n2d-highmem-4 include in-memory caching solutions like Redis, intermediate relational database management, data transformation pipelines, and application runtimes requiring substantial working memory alongside moderate parallel compute capacity.

It provides an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio with 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AES, VAES, and AVX instructions. In benchmark evaluations, the instance achieved average single-core performance with a Geekbench score of 1,426.0 and an encryption score of 4,247.89 in PassMark, though multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics reflect constraints common to 4-thread platforms. The configuration includes no local storage volumes and lacks dedicated GPU accelerators. This hardware setup suits memory-intensive workloads that require substantial operating memory without high parallel processor overhead, including in-memory datastores, relational databases, and batch data processing.
